messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] error with returnDeps=TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ruth,

we tried the new revision of RSiena (111) in which actors are also allowed
to decide not to toggle ties at each microstep.
All models seemed to work fine until we tried to extract the simulated
networks by specifying the option returnDeps=TRUE. This is the error message
we get:


Start phase 1
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(lapply(cl, recvResult)) :
  3 nodes produced errors; first error: The number 719 is not in the range
[0,719) of actors acting as receivers of ties


This occurs also for models whose simulated networks were already extracted
using previous RSiena revisions.
Please let us know if you can help us on this one.

Thanks a lot.

Marco

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] cross-network effects
messages.body_plain:
Dear Guido,

Basically, create the networks as normal, defining the node sets because 
you have a two-mode network. Then include both networks in the call to 
sienaDataCreate().

eg

friends1 <- as.matrix(read.table('friends_1.net'))
friends2 <- as.matrix(read.table('friends_2.net'))
projects1 <- as.matrix(read.table('projects1_r.net'))
projects2 <- as.matrix(read.table('projects2_r.net'))

friendship <- sienaNet(array(c(friends1, friends2), dim=c(75, 75, 2)), 
nodeSet="Friends")
projects <- sienaNet(array(c(projects1, projects2), dim=c(75, 60, 2)),
type='bipartite', nodeSet=c('Friends', 'Projs'))

Friends <- sienaNodeSet(75, 'Friends')
Projs <- sienaNodeSet(60, 'Projs')

mydata <- sienaDataCreate(friendship, projects, nodeSets=list(Friends, Projs))
myeff <- getEffects(mydata)

If you are using the siena01gui, just include two networks in the session.

Please let me know if this is not clear or it does not work (I adapted it 
so it is possible there are typos!).

Regards,

Ruth

messages.body_plain:
Hi Guido,

as addendum: if you want to have the effect for a dyadic covariate W, 
you can calculate the outdegree in the W network (or the square root of 
it) as an actor covariate outside RSiena, and use it as normal actor 
covariate in SienaDataCreate. The ego effect fior this covariate then 
expresses exactly what you need (the extent to which actors with high 
outdegrees on W will make more choices in the X network).

Christian

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Multiple networks
messages.body_plain:
Dear Paola,

You should be able to use something like
mynet1 <- sienaNet(array(c(s501, s502), dim=c(50, 50, 2)))
mynet2 <- sienaNet(array(c(s502, s503), dim=c(50, 50, 2)))
mydata <- sienaDataCreate(mynet1, mynet2)
myeff <- getEffects(mydata)
## for the first named network
myeff <- includeEffects(myeff, transTrip, balance)
## for other networks
myeff <- includeEffects(myeff, transTrip, balance, name='mynet2')

Effects that include two networks will need interaction1 set equal to the 
second network of the pair, with name specified if necessary (the default 
is the first network that appears in the effects object).

Please send me the code if you still cannot get it to work.

Regards,

Ruth
